text.p: Westmin Resources Ltd expects its C$307 million takeover of Gibraltar Mines Ltd to dilute earnings by 40 percent initially but then anticipates a sharp rise in profits and cash flow when Gibraltar's Lomas Bayas copper project in Chile begins production.

Westmin President Walter Segsworth told Reuters Tuesday that Westmin anticipates no problems arranging the rest of the financing for Lomas Bayas, which had been a major hurdle for Gibraltar, and plans to expand production by 50 percent within two years of the mine's projected full start-up in 1999.
"It's excellent," Segsworth said of the deal. Lomas Bayas "is a very, very low-cost project."

Gibraltar, based in Williams Lake, British Columbia, has agreed to the takeover and Placer Dome Inc, which was seeking to unload its 30.8 percent stake in Gibraltar, announced it would tender its shares to the deal.

Westmin will pay C$8.85 a share in cash and stock for Gibraltar, a significant premium over its closing share price of 6.30 last Friday. Segsworth said Westmin will issue about 29 million shares to finance the deal on top of its 67 million currently outstanding.
